clues.narrowing: Rules out coastal and desert towns; puts the player in a wide river valley ringed by low hills.

source.quote: Founded in 1842, it is located in the center of the Willamette Valley alongside the Willamette River, which runs north through the city.

clues.text: This city lies in the center of a wide river valley, beside a broad river that flows north. Low green hills ring the town on three sides.

clues.narrowing: Rules out even-rain lands; keeps the wet-winter, bone-dry-summer pattern.

source.quote: Rain is heaviest in late fall and throughout winter, and most of the annual precipitation falls between October and April, with a dry season from May through September.

clues.text: Rain pours down in late fall and winter here, under grey skies for weeks. Then summer turns bone dry, with scarce a drop for month after month.

clues.narrowing: Shrinks the list to the young town made territorial capital in 1851, lost briefly in 1855, then kept for good.

source.quote: In 1851, Salem became the territorial capital after it was moved from Oregon City . The capital was moved briefly to Corvallis in 1855, but was moved back to Salem permanently that same year.

clues.text: This town became the land's capital in 1851, just nine years after its start. It lost the role for a few months in 1855, then won it back for good.

clues.narrowing: Nearly decisive: the first lasting settlement here was a mission built in this valley in 1840.

source.quote: The first permanent American settlement in the area was the Jason Lee Methodist mission (1840)

clues.text: In 1840 the first lasting settlers built a mission in this green river valley. Farms and orchards soon spread across the rich flat land around it.

clues.narrowing: Confirms it: state lawmakers meet here, in the third capitol, topped by a gold pioneer.

source.quote: The third and current Oregon State Capitol was completed on the same site in 1938. It faces north instead of west like its predecessor, and is recognizable by its distinctive pioneer statue atop the capitol dome that is plated with gold-leaf

clues.text: Oregon law men meet in this city, in the state capitol. A gold statue of a first settler tops this third hall.

reveal.blurb: Mission settlers founded this valley town in 1842, and it became the capital of the territory in 1851. Two state houses here burned down; the building is the capitol, topped by a gold pioneer statue. Farms and cherry trees fill the green valley around it today. The city is the capital of the state: Salem is the capital of Oregon.
